text:
Maya Patel: Quick sync — we need to lock the dedicated capacity roadmap for the upcoming GA. Main items: reserved pool sizing, quota expiry semantics, surge-smoothing (soft preheat), and oncall gating for autoscale. Who can take the checklist?
Priya Iyer: I can take launch criteria + customer-facing constraints. Do we have an agreed SLA matrix?
Samir Chen: Not fully. Proposal: three tiers (bronze/silver/gold). Bronze = soft preheat only, Silver = guaranteed minimal burst, Gold = reserved headroom + prewarm.
Alex Gomez: Customer asks trending towards Gold for a few early enterprise pilots. They want predictable 99th pct latency during surges.
Evan Liu: Ops note — Gold requires oncall gating and quick drain policies. We need a drain path that hits <2s cold-start for fallback. Also need runbook updates.
Maya Patel: Agree. Priya, add explicit launch blockers: runbook, billing mapping for burst credits, SLA wording.
Priya Iyer: Will do. Quick Q: how do we want quota expiry to behave? auto-renew vs explicit reclaim? Customers want some carryover.
Samir Chen: Suggestion: quota windows with optional carryover up to 20% for Silver/Gold; Bronze = expire. Also an opt-in 'burst carryover' toggle.
Alex Gomez: Legal asked for clear cutoff if we need to preempt for emergency maintenance. Add a clause for 72-hour notice for reclaiming reserved capacity.
Evan Liu: From SRE — what does surge-smoothing look like technically? We proposed a small elastic buffer + preheat window. Example config we tested: 
```
reserved_pool: gold-us-east-1
buffer_tokens: 0.12
preheat_window: 60s
burst_policy: allow_up_to_2x_for_30s
drain_timeout: 45s
```
This kept p99 within SLA during simulated spikes.
Maya Patel: Nice. Samir, can your team own producing the default `buffer_tokens`/`preheat_window` table per instance class?
Samir Chen: Yep. We'll run experiments for seq_len 128, 512, 2048 and publish profiles.
Priya Iyer: For launch checklist: (1) SLA doc draft, (2) billing mapping + invoice examples, (3) runbook + oncall playbook, (4) observability dashboard per pool, (5) customer opt-in flow.
Alex Gomez: Add customer comms + pilot acceptance criteria: pilot must hit four 24h surge windows with p99 < target and no unplanned preemptions.
Evan Liu: Ops gating: require oncall runbook and a canary for region-level preemption. If canary fails, autoscale must fallback to spare shared pools.
Maya Patel: Ok owners: Priya = launch docs & pilot criteria; Samir = sizing + profiles; Alex = customer comms + contract clause; Evan = runbook + ops gating; Maya = overall signoff. I'll schedule an alignment call Fri 9am PT.
ops-bot: Deployment checker: next deploy window Fri 10:00 PT. Reminder: update "dedicated-pools" runbook before deploy.
Alex Gomez: :thumbsup: Adding one more ask — we should expose a self-serve slider for carryover (0-20%) in Console. Product design follow-up?
Maya Patel: Good idea; log as product task. Priya, can you slot Console mockups into the pilot docs?
Priya Iyer: Will do.
Samir Chen: One more tech risk: KV cache prewarm increases memory footprint. We'll include a memory/burst tradeoff table in the profiles doc.
Evan Liu: A note on alerts: add a fractional-burst alert when >75% of buffer_tokens used for >60s. That should trigger paging.
Maya Patel: Perfect. Thanks team. I'll put this thread summary into the roadmap ticket and link owners. Meeting invite sent.
Alex Gomez: Thanks — looking forward to the Fri sync.
Priya Iyer: I'll draft the SLA and share by EOD Thu.
Samir Chen: Running final perf sweeps today. Will post results here.
Evan Liu: I'll update the oncall checklist and add canary smoke tests to the release job.
ops-bot: Note added to ticket #RDW-4321: "oncall gating required for Gold pools"
Maya Patel: Closing thread for now, will reopen after Fri meeting if needed.
